## RLS posture — ⭐ re-measured 2026-08-25 (RLS SECTION ONLY)

⚠ **This section carries its own stamp, and it is NEWER than the file-level "Last generated" above.**
Only the RLS/security figures below were re-read from the live DB on 2026-08-25; the rest of this file
still dates from its 2026-08-22 regeneration. **Do not read this stamp as a whole-file refresh** — that
conflation is exactly what this file's header warns about.

- Public base tables: **372** (2026-08-25; was 340 on 2026-07-28, 290 on 2026-07-16, 245 on 2026-06-30,
  88 in older CLAUDE.md prose — the count drifts upward as tables are added; treat the exact number as
  informational, the invariant below is the fact that matters). Public views: **136**. Public
  materialized views: **34**.
  ⓘ 2026-09-03: **+1 since this stamp** — `mv_candy_scarcity_board` (behind the `candy_scarcity_board` wrapper, anon/authenticated REVOKED, migration `20260903221326`). Re-measure; do not add to the 34 by hand.
  ⓘ 2026-09-04: **+1 TABLE since this stamp** — `public.pipeline_gap_hourly` (hour, pipeline, p50_gap_min, expected_ticks, ticks, max_gap_min, skipped_ticks, scheduled_pipelines, pipelines_with_skips, silent_pipelines, computed_at; PK (hour, pipeline); RLS on, service_role SELECT only), written hourly by `rollup_pipeline_gaps(integer)` (SECDEF, anon/auth revoked) from pg_cron jobid 443. Migration `20260904024810`.
  ⚠ The 2026-08-25 data-quality sweep reported **367** base tables; a live read the same day returns
  **372**. Neither is wrong — they are two dated samples of a moving count. **Re-measure; quote neither.**
- ✅ **Tables with `rowsecurity=false`: 0 as of 2026-08-25 — the invariant holds again.** The 08-22 red
  entry was **`series_detail_rollup`**, and it is **RESOLVED**: RLS is now enabled on the table
  (`relrowsecurity = true`, verified live). ⚠ **The 08-22 assessment was correct and is worth preserving:**
  that red was an **INSTRUMENT** problem, not a measured exposure — the table's migration had already
  revoked all anon/authenticated privileges, and its only reader `get_series_detail` is SECURITY DEFINER
  (which bypasses RLS anyway), so no anon-reachable path ever existed. The fix closed the instrument, not
  a hole. **A standing red instrument trains people to skim past it, which is the documented failure
  class** — that is why closing it mattered even though nothing was exposed.
- **RLS-on is NOT the whole posture** (the 2026-07-19 Panini/Candy lesson): Supabase's
  default per-role `anon`/`authenticated` grant survives `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC`, so a
  table can be RLS-on and still readable at `/rest/v1/<table>`. The live checks that cover
  that class, all re-run 2026-08-25 — **all five clean**:

  | check | return shape | clean reading | 2026-08-25 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `check_public_security_invariants()` | SETOF | **0 rows** | ✅ 0 |
  | `check_anon_write_surface()` | SETOF | **0 rows** | ✅ 0 |
  | `check_secdef_anon_exec_drift()` | scalar jsonb | **array length 0** | ✅ 0 |
  | `check_secdef_anon_execute_violations()` | scalar jsonb | **array length 0** | ✅ 0 |
  | `check_cursor_stall_threshold_drift()` | scalar jsonb | **array length 0** | ✅ 0 |

  ⚠ **Read the RETURN SHAPE before interpreting the count.** A SETOF check is 0-rows-clean; a
  scalar-jsonb check returns **`count(*) = 1` when clean** — read the array LENGTH, never the row count.
  Both shapes are mixed inside this one table, which is why the distinction has to be re-derived per
  function rather than remembered per file.
- ⚠ **`check_public_security_invariants()` now has SIX arms**, not the five it shipped with: RLS-off /
  anon-write base tables · updatable+writable views · unexpected-definer views · anon-EXECUTE secdef
  trigger fns · and (added `20260824233704`) **anon-readable materialized views**. That sixth arm exists
  because `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` grants `postgres`-created MVs `anon=rxm`, so **every new
  materialized view is born anon-readable**. 🔓 **Still open:** the arm DETECTS an exposed MV, it does not
  PREVENT one — stripping `anon=rxm` from the schema default privileges is the root fix and is Trevor's
  call. ⛔ `information_schema.role_table_grants` returns **0 rows for all 34 MVs** while they demonstrably
  hold grants, so any guard reading MV grants through it passes **vacuously**.

## Regeneration SQL (read-only)

```sql
-- FMV-home table existence
SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public'
  AND tablename = ANY (ARRAY['pinnacle_fmv_snapshots','pinnacle_fmv_snapshots_backup_20260608',
    'pinnacle_fmv_history','pinnacle_catalog','fmv_snapshots']) ORDER BY tablename;

-- pinnacle_catalog FMV columns
SELECT column_name FROM information_schema.columns
  WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name='pinnacle_catalog' AND column_name LIKE 'fmv%' ORDER BY 1;

-- enums
SELECT t.typname, array_agg(e.enumlabel ORDER BY e.enumsortorder)
  FROM pg_type t JOIN pg_enum e ON e.enumtypid=t.oid
  WHERE t.typname IN ('fmv_confidence','tier_type','chain_type','edition_kind') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

-- RLS posture. NOTE: rls_off_count=0 is necessary but NOT sufficient — the default
-- anon/authenticated grant survives REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC, so also run both live invariants.
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public') AS public_tables,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_views  WHERE schemaname='public') AS public_views,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public' AND rowsecurity=false) AS rls_off_count,
       (SELECT array_agg(tablename ORDER BY tablename) FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public' AND rowsecurity=false) AS rls_off_tables,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM public.check_public_security_invariants()) AS security_invariant_rows,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM public.check_anon_write_surface()) AS anon_write_rows;

-- collections registry
SELECT id, slug, name, chain, is_active FROM public.collections ORDER BY slug;

-- existence sweep for every table CLAUDE.md names (edit the VALUES list to match the doc)
WITH named(t) AS (VALUES ('editions'),('pinnacle_editions'),('wallet_moments_cache'),('fmv_snapshots'),
  ('sales'),('badge_editions'),('flowty_transactions'),('flowty_loans'),('flowty_loan_events'),
  ('players'),('sets'),('linked_accounts'),('collections'),('pinnacle_sales'),('pinnacle_catalog'),
  ('pinnacle_fmv_history'),('moments'),('pipeline_runs'),('pipeline_cadence_watchlist'),
  ('pipeline_run_locks'),('topshot_moment_subeditions'),('unmapped_sales'),('cached_listings'),
  ('cached_listings_v2'),('topshot_active_listings'),('analytics_sales'))
SELECT n.t,
  (p.tablename IS NOT NULL) AS base_table,
  (v.viewname IS NOT NULL) AS is_view
FROM named n
  LEFT JOIN pg_tables p ON p.schemaname='public' AND p.tablename=n.t
  LEFT JOIN pg_views  v ON v.schemaname='public' AND v.viewname=n.t
  ORDER BY base_table, n.t;

-- editions column count (CLAUDE.md cites "32 columns") + sales partitions
SELECT
  (SELECT count(*) FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name='editions') AS editions_cols,
  (SELECT array_agg(tablename ORDER BY tablename) FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public' AND tablename ~ '^sales_[0-9]{4}$') AS sales_partitions;
```

## Disney Pinnacle grain — which table answers which question (2026-09-26)

Measured live 2026-09-26 PT; re-derive before quoting a number. Case history: [known-issues #150](known-issues.md).

| Question | Answer from | NOT from |
|---|---|---|
| What pins exist / what a pin is (art, set, variant, series, FMV, floor) | `pinnacle_catalog` — one row per PIN, `render_id` PK (2,732 rows) | `pinnacle_editions` |
| Which pins a character / franchise has | `pinnacle_catalog.characters[]` / `.franchises[]` (arrays: a duo pin names both; a pin can name several franchises) | `pinnacle_editions.character_name` / `.franchise` (ONE per row) |
| Which pins a wallet holds | `wallet_moments_cache.render_id` (set on 41,264 of 41,264 Pinnacle rows, every one a catalog `render_id`) | `wallet_moments_cache.edition_key` for a per-pin question |
| A sale's pin | `pinnacle_sales.render_id` (200,205 of 200,214) — `idx_pinnacle_sales_render_id` | a join through `pinnacle_editions` |
| Set-level legacy key (`ROYALTY:Variant:Printing`) | `pinnacle_editions.id` (= `pinnacle_catalog.legacy_edition_key` = `wallet_moments_cache.edition_key`) | ⛔ `pinnacle_editions.external_id` — set on 31 of 594 rows and equal to NONE of the 431 keys wallets hold |

- ⛔ **`pinnacle_editions` is SET-LEVEL:** one legacy key can span several characters and pins; the row names ONE of them. A page built on it under-counts (Star Wars franchise 129 of 723 pins; series 2026 11 of 1,023), and a `thumbnail_url IS NOT NULL` filter on it drops whole characters (Aurora). It is also only as complete as the wallet walks that write it — `pinnacle_editions_fill_from_catalog()` (pg_cron `rpc-pinnacle-editions-fill-from-catalog`, 07:43 UTC daily) back-fills rows, thumbnails and `players` rows from the catalog.
- **Matching rules the fixed functions share (copy them, do not re-invent):** franchise = `btrim(regexp_replace(fr, '[™®©]', '', 'g'))` over `unnest(franchises)` (the catalog spells some "Star Wars™"; stripped names equal the ones `pinnacle_editions`/`players` use, so the team layout's canonical-slug redirect keeps comparing equal); character = exact `lower(btrim())` over `unnest(characters)`, OR for a duo name ("Maurice & Cogsworth") the joined list with `' & '` / `' '`.
- **Pattern for moving a Pinnacle branch:** read the catalog first; fall through to the old `pinnacle_editions` read ONLY when the catalog does not name the subject (e.g. "20th Century Studios", 1 legacy row), so no page that resolved before stops resolving.
- **Functions on the catalog as of 2026-09-26:** `get_player_editions`, `get_player_detail`, `get_player_top_sales`, `get_series_editions`, `get_series_rollups`, `get_series_detail`, `refresh_series_detail_rollup`, `get_team_detail`, `get_team_top_editions`, `get_team_players`, `get_team_checklist`, `get_team_checklist_progress`, `get_team_sets`, `get_team_activity`, `pinnacle_top_editions`, `pinnacle_top_sales`, `pinnacle_tier_analytics`, `pinnacle_daily_tier_volume`, `get_pinnacle_franchise_breakdown`, `get_edition_detail` (render_id; a multi-character legacy key names its SET), `get_platform_stats`, `analytics_sets_summary`; set pages via `sets_summary` (catalog-only sets + catalog spellings in `set_name_variants`). `get_team_squeeze` is Top Shot-only by design. Still reading `pinnacle_editions`, measured harmless (known-issues #150): `get_user_top_owned_moments` (image fallback never reached), `collection_readiness` (row-exists check), `get_pinnacle_set_progress` (no caller). The fill/ingest writers (`pinnacle_editions_fill_from_catalog`, `upsert_pinnacle_edition`, backfills) maintain the table itself.
- ⓘ `pinnacle_editions` holds **148 numeric-id rows** (one-off 2026-04-16 batch, set "Unknown") that anchor 1,289 `pinnacle_sales` rows by FK — do not delete.
- ⓘ The image resolver `/api/public/pinnacle-image/<render_id>` 302s to the signed CDN render; `?v=thumb` serves the cropped ~285 KB render (list views), the default the ~1.1 MB full render. `pinnacle_catalog.thumbnail_url` is always that resolver path.
- ⭐ **Live listings (2026-09-27): `pinnacle_live_listings`** (`price_usd` in DOLLARS — ⚠ the GraphQL `listing.price` is raw UFix64 × 1e8; the route divides, and the first sweep shipped without it) — every listing Disney's Studio GraphQL returned on the catalog floor sweep's last COMPLETE pass (`/api/admin/backfill-pinnacle-catalog`, 5×/day, ~16.1k listings, 161 pages). Written by `pinnacle_live_listings_replace(p_rows, p_seen_at)` (upsert first, then delete rows the sweep did not return; the route calls it only when the sweep reached `hasNextPage=false`). Read by the Sniper through `get_pinnacle_live_listings_for_sniper(p_limit)` (joined to `pinnacle_catalog`, each listing priced by its OWN render). Service-role only. Migration `20260927175154`.
- ⛔ **Not a live-listing source: `cached_listings_v2` (source `direct`) for Pinnacle.** It is the on-chain ListingAvailable/Completed event feed — a change-only feed, not a census (#149). Measured 2026-09-27: 18,546 "open" Pinnacle rows vs ~16.1k live on the marketplace, and where the seller's wallet is indexed, 263 of 751 "open" listings were for pins the seller no longer held. ⛔ **And not Flowty** — `lib/pinnacle/pinnacleFlowty.ts` still exists (the ingest route reads it) but the marketplace closed 2026-05-13; until 09-27 the Sniper read it and showed 2 deals from 2026-08-21.
- ⚠ **`wallet_moments_cache.is_locked = true` on Pinnacle rows is REAL: the contract's own `Pinnacle.NFT.isLocked()`** — a pin from a maturing edition cannot move until its maturity date (`/api/cron/lock-check-batch`, `PINNACLE_LOCK_SCRIPT`; ~375 rows on 09-27, 20–30 wallets/day). **Trevor, 2026-09-27: KEEP the data and the daily check; show NO lock UI on any Pinnacle page** (`collectionHasLocking()` in `lib/collections.ts`). ⛔ Do not clear the rows or drop `disney_pinnacle` from the lock lane; if it is ever surfaced, the word is "Maturing", not "Locked".
- ⛔ **WRITERS obey the grain too (2026-09-27, [known-issues #151](known-issues.md)).** `wallet_moments_cache.player_name` for Pinnacle is written by `backfill_pinnacle_wmc_metadata_from_editions` from `pinnacle_catalog` by `render_id`: the pin's `characters[]` as a list ("Poe Dameron & BB-8", "Simba, Timon & Pumbaa"), else the pin's TITLE for an object/scene pin with no character ("Piston Cup", 15 catalog rows). `wallet_moments_cache.character_name` = `pinnacle_catalog.character_name` = **the pin's title**, not a character ("Master Yoda" on a Yoda pin, "Carefree Companions" on Simba/Timon/Pumbaa). Until 09-27 the writer used the set-level key: 769 rows read 'Unknown', ~31k another character from the same set; 33,000 repaired. Pin: `supabase/tests/backfill_pinnacle_wmc_metadata_from_editions.sql`.

## Trophy-case campaign tracking (2026-09-27)

Built for the trophy-case campaign ([ledger](../overnight/ledger.md), 2026-09-27). All service-role only (RLS on, anon/authenticated revoked). Migration `20260927154432_audit_20260927_trophy_case_campaign_tracking`.

| Object | What it is |
|---|---|
| `trophy_case_milestones` | One row per user: SET-ONCE `started_at` (first pin) and `completed_at` (first time 6/6 slots filled), each with a `*_source` of `observed` (stamped by the trigger when it happened) or `backfill_upper_bound` (7 users reconstructed 09-27 from overwritten `pinned_at` values — the true moment is AT OR BEFORE it). Written by the SECDEF trigger `trophy_case_milestones_track` on `trophy_moments` (INSERT or UPDATE OF moment_id), so every writer is covered, incl. an authenticated user writing through RLS and `reorder_trophy_slots`' delete-and-reinsert. |
| `funnel_events.user_id` + `trophy_pinned` / `trophy_removed` | Written ONLY by `/api/profile/trophy` (service role) after the write lands, with the client's session id + attribution (`getFunnelContext()` in `lib/track-funnel.ts`); an unpin logs only if a row was removed. The anon/authenticated INSERT policy refuses both types and any non-null `user_id`, so the public beacon cannot forge one. `surface` = `trophy-case:slot-N`. |
| `internal_accounts` | PRESENCE = the account is ours (founder, brand, Claude QA). Absence means "not reviewed as internal", not "verified external". ⛔ **Exclude it from every traction / campaign count, and insert any QA account you create in the same turn.** Rows are data (inserted by `execute_sql`); the emails that identify them stay out of the public repo. |
| `trophy_case_campaign_users` | Per user: milestones + `is_internal` + current slots + first-pin campaign (`first_pin_utm_source/_medium/_campaign/_share_ref` parsed from the first `trophy_pinned` event's referrer). `first_pin_*` NULL for pre-09-27 pins = UNKNOWN, not unattributed. |
| `trophy_case_campaign_daily` | Starts/completions per PACIFIC day, internal split out, `includes_backfill` flags reconstructed days. |

- ⚠ `trophy_moments.pinned_at` is OVERWRITTEN by every re-pin (POST upserts the row) and an unpin DELETEs the row — never read either as "when the case was started". Use the milestones table.
- UI: `/admin/trophy-campaign` (RPC_ADMIN_TOKEN) over `/api/admin/trophy-campaign`, which FAILS rather than degrades on any read (a partial auth-user walk would move real accounts into "not started" — the list an operator emails).
- ⭐ **Pinnacle entity keys (2026-09-27, measured).** A character page is keyed by the `characters` TRAIT (513/513 resolve since trigger `pinnacle_catalog_ensure_character_players_trg`, 20260928111652, gives every trait value a `players` row), NOT `character_name` — that is the PIN's name ("Welcome to Endor" = Ewok + Wicket) and 266/683 have no page, so on Pinnacle a row's name links the PIN. A franchise page is keyed with ™/®/© dropped ("Star Wars™" → `/team/star-wars`; the raw slug 404s) — `lib/entity-href.ts` `pinnacleFranchiseHref`. Set pages resolve for Pinnacle since 09-26 (`setEntityHref` links them). `/disney-pinnacle/edition/<id>` is a 308 to `/pinnacle/moment/<id>` (next.config) — link the target (`editionRouteHref`). Set "Total Mint" = SUM of the pins' `total_minted` (`get_set_detail`, 20260928064405; sets_summary's figure is ONE set-level key's). Character mint dates only when EVERY `pinnacle_editions` row is dated (83/594 are; 20260928064804). `pinnacle_sales.serial_number`: NULL by design on Open / Open Event / Starter pins; for serialised pins it is filled by `pinnacle_sale_serials_tick` (pg_cron, every 10 min: local sources, then Studio-GraphQL history via pg_net — #156).
- ⭐ **Render FMV = the RECENCY-WEIGHTED MEDIAN (2026-09-27, #155).** `pinnacle_fmv_recalc_render` prices each render at the weighted median of its 90-day sales (weights exp(-0.03×days)); `fmv_wap_usd` stays the untrimmed weighted mean. The old WAP-centred 0.33×–3× trim dropped a FALLING render's recent sales as outliers (Minnie $21.56 vs $3/$6 sales). Pinned: `supabase/tests/pinnacle_fmv_recalc_render.sql`.
- ⭐ **Serial premium = #1 and PERFECT only (Trevor, 2026-09-27 — the shared `serial_fmv_estimate` pattern).** `pinnacle_serial_fmv_multipliers` bands are `first` / `perfect` (#N of N, mint > 1) / `normal`; the old top-5% / top-20% bands are gone. Fitted weekly by `compute_pinnacle_serial_fmv_multipliers` (Sun 12:00 UTC; 09-27 refit: first ×14.45 n=50, perfect ×3.49 n=36). One implementation per side: SQL `pinnacle_serial_fmv_estimate` ⇄ TS `lib/pinnacle/serial-fmv.ts` (cross-agreement test). Surfaces claim a premium only over a HIGH/MEDIUM base FMV and only at mint ≥ 25, and publish it as the shared `SerialFmvData` badge (`pinnacleSerialFmvData`) — Collection table, Sniper, pin-page ladder.
